lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 5.d4
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 d4 d5 Bd3 Bd6 O-O O-O

teaching.intro: White puts a pawn on d4. Black's knight on e4 still needs support. A pawn on d5 can guard it while contesting the center.
replies: The bishop on d3 now attacks your knight on e4. Your d5-pawn already protects it, so you can develop your bishop.
White has moved the king away from the center. Your f8-bishop and g8-knight have moved too, so you can castle on the same side.

notes: Attack the knight on e5 with a pawn.
Chase the knight first. If it retreats to f3, you can recover the pawn on e4.
White's knight retreated. What can your knight take?
Recover the e4-pawn with your knight.
Use a pawn to support your knight on e4.

Develop the bishop next to your king.
The bishop comes to an active square and clears the way to castle.

Castle and finish the opening with your king safe.

lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 5.Nc3
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 Nc3 Nxc3 dxc3 Be7 Bd3 O-O

teaching.intro: White's new knight on c3 attacks yours on e4. A trade on c3 changes the pawn structure and gives White a half-open d-file.
replies: White's d-pawn took back. The two white c-pawns share a file, and the c1-bishop now has an open diagonal through d2. Both sides can develop quickly.
White's bishop comes to d3 and looks toward h7. You can castle and then watch for White's other bishop joining the attack.

notes: Attack the knight on e5 with a pawn.
Chase the knight first, then look to recover the pawn.
White's knight retreated. What can your knight take?
Recover the pawn on e4.
White's new knight attacks your e4-knight. Can you trade them?
Trade on c3. White can recapture with a pawn, and you can finish development.
Clear the bishop out of the way of castling.
Develop the bishop to e7 and prepare to castle.
Your kingside is clear.
Castle. White can bring a queen or rook to the half-open d-file, where your d6-pawn is a target.

lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 5.Qe2
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nf3 Nxe4 Qe2 Qe7 d3 Nf6 Nc3 Nc6

teaching.intro: White's queen on e2 attacks your knight along the e-file. From e7 your queen can defend that same knight, so a capture on e4 can be answered with a capture.
replies: The pawn on d3 adds a second attacker to e4. Moving the knight back to f6 saves it while your queen stays on the e-file.
White develops the b1-knight and adds control of e4. Your b8-knight can develop too and contest d4 and e5.

notes: Attack the knight on e5 with a pawn.
Chase the knight first, then look to recover the pawn.
White's knight retreated. What can your knight take?
Recover the pawn on e4.
White's queen attacks your knight. Use your queen to defend it.
Meet Qe2 with Qe7. If White takes on e4, your queen can take back.
The d-pawn now attacks your knight too. Return it to a familiar square.
Retreat to f6. Your queen covers the e-file.
Develop the queenside knight.
Bring out the b8-knight and add control of the center.

lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 4.Nxf7
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nxf7 Kxf7 d4 c5 Nc3 cxd4 Qxd4 Nc6

teaching.intro: White's knight on f7 attacks both the queen on d8 and the rook on h8. Your king can capture that knight, but the king will have to stay in the center for now.
replies: White builds a center with pawns on d4 and e4 and opens the diagonal for the c1-bishop. A push to c5 attacks the d4-pawn directly.
White's knight develops to c3 and supports e4. Exchanging your c-pawn for the d4-pawn reduces White's central space.
White's queen has recaptured on d4. Your b8-knight can develop to c6 with an attack on that queen.

notes: Attack the knight on e5 with a pawn.
Chase the knight. Be ready if it takes on f7 instead of retreating.
The knight on f7 forks your queen and rook. Can your king take it?
Take the knight. You give up castling rights, so watch White's central pawns.
Which pawn can attack White's d4-pawn from the side?
Play ...c5 to challenge White's center before it builds an attack.
Your c-pawn can trade for a central pawn.
Take on d4. If the queen recaptures, you can develop with tempo.
Develop a knight that attacks the queen on d4.

lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 4.Nd3
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nd3 Nxe4 Nf4 Nf6 d4 Be7 Bd3 c5

teaching.intro: White's knight went to d3 instead of f3. It still does not guard e4, and it now blocks White's d-pawn. Your f6-knight can take on e4.
replies: White moves the knight again to f4, freeing the d-pawn. You can return your knight to f6 and control d5.
White advances to d4, claiming space. Developing your f8-bishop gets your king ready to castle.
White's bishop on d3 looks toward h7. With your kingside clear, you also have time in this line to challenge the d4-pawn with ...c5.

notes: Make the e5-knight move.
The d6-pawn attacks White's knight on e5.

The bishop on e7 clears f8 and supports the knight on f6.

lines.name: 3.Nxe5 · 4.Nc4
lines.moves: Nxe5 d6 Nc4 Nxe4 d4 d5 Ne3 Nf6 c4 dxc4 Nc3 Nc6

teaching.intro: The c4-knight does not protect e4. After you take the e4-pawn, ...d5 can support your knight and attack White's knight on c4 in the same move.
replies: White plays d4 to take space in the center. From d5 your pawn can attack the c4-knight and protect your e4-knight.

lines.name: 3.Bc4 · Bishop comes out early
lines.moves: Bc4 Nxe4 d3 Nf6 Nxe5 d5 Bb3 Bd6

teaching.intro: White's bishop looks at f7 and the knight on f3 attacks e5. The white pawn on e4 has no defender, so your f6-knight can take it.

Develop the bishop so it attacks the knight on e5.

teaching.intro: White's bishop on d3 guards e4, so the f6-knight cannot win that pawn. You can play ...d5 to challenge the pawn instead. If White takes on d5, ...e4 hits both the bishop and knight.
